data.chip: No part number. « Burr Brown D/A converters in a digital symmetric configuration », preceded by « an algorithm from the highly regarded Anagram Technologies ». The count of converters is not stated.

source.quote: Soulution's own page for the 560, read 2026-11-24. Table headed « Bit depth/sampling rage max » (the misspelling is the page's): « AES/EBU: 24 bit/192 kHz »; « SPDIF: 24 bit/192 kHz »; « Optical: 24 bit/96 kHz »; « USB: 24 bit/384 kHz, 1 bit/5.64 MHz »; « Network: 24 bit/384 kHz, 1 bit/5.64 MHz ». Digital inputs listed as « AES/EBU, SPDIF-RCA, Optical, USB, Network ». On the conversion stage: « Burr-Brown devices perform D/A conversion only. Their internal upsampling and filter stages are not used. » and « Our players and D/A converters use an algorithm from the highly regarded Anagram Technologies followed by Burr Brown D/A converters in a digital symmetric configuration. » On the signal path: « Audio data is buffered then upsampled to 24Bit/384kHz. » On the analogue stage: « The 560's 3rd order bessel filter, with a cut-off frequency of 120kHz, does show a phase shift of up to 15 degrees in the audio band. » and « Due to the Zero-Phase-Technology the phase error of the analog music signal remains below 1 degree, 20Hz - 100kHz! ». Self-description: « soulution 560 D/A converter » and « The 560 D/A-Converter does excell at exactly this task. It captures all digital music data and transports it in the analog domain. »

open_doubt.text: Whether this device reconverts DSD to PCM. The temptation is strong and the page does not close it. « Audio data is buffered then upsampled to 24Bit/384kHz » describes the signal path with no exception; the inputs accept « 1 bit/5.64 MHz »; the output of that stage is stated as 24-bit PCM. Read together they say DSD arrives, meets a PCM upsampler and leaves as 24/384 - which would make dsd_reconverted_to_pcm true. But « Audio data » is the maker's word for everything it had been talking about, which was PCM, and the sentence never says the 1-bit stream takes that path. No fact is written. Getting this field wrong is expensive: it is what tells an engine whether sending DSD to this device is worth anything at all, and the cascade carries it almost everywhere: re-measured 2026-11-24, 56 of the 59 records that resolve it at all take it from their family, 3 from evidence of their own.
open_doubt.what_would_resolve_it: One sentence from Soulution about what happens to a 1-bit input, or a manual. Failing that, a measurement: feed DSD128 and look for the PCM signature. Do NOT resolve it by reading the upsampling sentence harder.

data._aliases_typed: Typed 2026-11-24. An untyped alias list merged three different things and one of them is dangerous: a SPELLING is the same object written differently, an EDITION is a variant of this model that no fact yet distinguishes, and a NEIGHBOUR is a DIFFERENT PRODUCT resolved here only because it has no record of its own. Before typing, a match on "Spring 2" would have asserted the Spring 3's facts for another generation, and "HA 200" - a headphone amplifier - sat beside the DAC 200 as if it were the same device. They are listed together because they share one USB identity. THE RELATIONS WERE ASSIGNED FROM PRODUCT KNOWLEDGE, NOT FROM A CITED SOURCE: a neighbour is the claim that two things are different devices, which deserves evidence like any other, and aliases live in identity where the evidence rule does not reach. Contest them.

data.chip: No converter chip: « R2R DAC technology using 600 pieces of 0.01% VAR Bulk Metal Foil resistors Vishay Foil Resistors », « the famous naked Vishay foil ». The maker counts its resistors and names their tolerance and their supplier, which is more than any chip datasheet in this catalogue says about its own silicon - and still gives no ladder bit depth, the field that is known for 7 records of 61.

device_settings.name: Non-oversampling DAC compensation filter
device_settings.why_it_matters: A filter the listener can switch off. Second such setting in this catalogue after RME's five DA filters, and the second argument that internal_bypass - which assumes a RATE threshold - is modelled for the rarer shape.

open_doubt.text: KEPT ON PURPOSE, against the move that took its two neighbours out. This record shares their identity - brand "unknown", model "unknown" - and it is not the same kind of thing. Its source says so: « Not a device. The record the engine uses when the driver reports an identity no record matches and the listener has not said. » It is the TERMINAL of the cascade, the bottom a consumer resolves to when nothing else matches, and deleting it would remove the floor rather than a duplicate. akm-generique and ess-generique were chip defaults wearing a device; this one is the absence of a device, which is a role no chip family can fill.
open_doubt.what_is_doubtful: Its `kind` says "dac", which is the one field that is plainly wrong: it is not a converter, it is the answer "we do not know which converter". And it carries dsd_direct false where its chip family says "unknown" - both end in the conservative branch, so nothing breaks, but two levels still disagree. The real question is whether a terminal belongs in devices/ at all, or whether a consumer should get it from the vocabulary instead of from a record that has to pretend to be a device to exist.

data.chip: No part number, and the maker goes out of its way not to give one: « a chosen DAC chip », corrected from outside by a « Dual-differential musIC 3 128-bit-feed-forward error correction process », with « Processing is done at 128 bit internal resolution ». So bought silicon, deliberately unnamed, with the maker's own correction ahead of it.

source.quote: Wadax's own page for the Atlantis Reference DAC, read 2026-11-24. Specification block, « Inputs: »: « USB (32-384KHz, 16-24-32 bits, DSD64, DSD128, DSD256, MQA) »; « 2xSPDIF RCA (32KHz-192KHz, 16-24 bits) »; « 2xSPDIF BNC (32KHz-192KHz, 16-24 bits) »; « 2xAES-EBU (32KHz-192KHz, 16-24 bits) »; « Native Reference Wadax Link (native PCM, DSD), 3xAES-EBU, 1 RJ45 »; « Optional: WADAX Akasa Optical Module ». On the processing: « By mapping the error mechanisms of a chosen DAC chip under load using Adaptive Delta Hilbert Mapping »; « Dual-differential musIC 3 128-bit-feed-forward error correction process »; « Processing is done at 128 bit internal resolution »; « Zepto Reference clock: doubled the master clock frequency with only 12fs total jitter. »; « including native DSD replay over our proprietary triple AES-EBU connection ». Self-description: « The Atlantis REFERENCE DAC is our response to these findings, with lower levels of clock noise and significant improvements in PSU and mechanical isolation. » and « The result is the most accurate and most musically satisfying DAC ever designed. » The page also carries spec images at images/dacConnectivity.png and images/dacInNumbers.png, not opened: the text above is the page's own.

open_doubt.text:
TWO DOUBTS, AND THE FIRST IS THE MOST VALUABLE QUESTION IN THIS CATALOGUE.
1. Weiss writes « The unit can also convert DSD audio to PCM and offers a digital output in AES/EBU format. » If that means DSD is re-converted internally before analogue conversion, dsd_reconverted_to_pcm is true and a consumer should never send this device DSD. If it means the unit can transcode DSD to PCM for its AES/EBU digital output, the field is untouched. The sentence supports both readings. One email to Weiss settles it - which is exactly the inlet this catalogue rates highest and has never used.
2. The ES9028PRO is stated for « the MK2 version » only. By this catalogue's own rule an edition becomes a record of its own the day a fact distinguishes it, and a different converter board is such a fact. So DAC204-MK2 has earned a record - the first alias typed `edition` to do so - and what the pre-MK2 used is unknown. Nine households own a « DAC204 » with no generation stated.
